# Re-entry Navigation Case Plan: Christopher Barranco

## 1. Clinical Risk & Criminogenic Profile
- **LS/CMI Score:** 21 / 43 (High Risk / Need Category)
- **Primary Domain (ADP - 5/8):** Chronic substance use starting at age 13; severe relapse driver for all historic criminal offenses.
- **Secondary Domain (EE - 5/9):** Associate's Degree in Accounting (Midlands Tech) and trade expertise in gutter installation/roofing; however, lack of stable 12-month payroll and recent unemployment elevate risk.
- **Tertiary Domain (PA/AP - 2/4):** Active property/shoplifting offending within the last 12 months scores supportive of crime, requiring CBT focus on cognitive distortions.
- **Protective Strengths:** Oxford House President, active church volunteer/usher, formal accounting education, high trade skill set.

## 2. Immediate Clinical Triage & Legal Stabilization
1. **Probation Warrant Mitigation:** Coordinate directly with Agent Burgess (Kershaw PPP) to present Turn90 progress and establish a formal compliance agreement.
2. **Lexington DUS Resolution:** Engage SC Legal Services and Midlands Fatherhood Coalition to address pending DUS 1st court date and structure a manageable SCDMV payment plan.
3. **Debt Management:** Utilize his accounting background to co-create a 'Debt Snowball' budget targeting his $3,500 debt to Landmark, alleviating financial anxiety.

## 3. Workplace & Facilitation Plan
- **Facilitation Protocol:** Use neutral curiosity (Standard 1.5) and trauma-informed collaborative coaching. Avoid confrontational directives.
- **Workplace Vetting:** Match only with verified drug-free employers (e.g., commercial maintenance, structural steel, or warehouse logistics) that respect physical lung limitations and maintain prosocial peer cultures.

# My Fresh Start Action & Resource Guide: Christopher Barranco

Welcome to your First Shift re-entry blueprint, Christopher. Your strengths—your leadership as Oxford House President, your Midlands Tech accounting degree, and your expert trade skills in specialized installation and machinery—are the foundation of your fresh start. This guide outlines local Columbia resources and vetted second-chance employers to support your goals.

---

## 1. Key Community Resources & Legal Stabilization

- **Midlands Fatherhood Coalition (License Reinstatement & Legal Support)**
  - **Services:** Driver's license reinstatement counseling, SCDMV payment plans, and child support court advocacy.
  - **Contact:** (803) 933-0530 | 1821 Hampton St, Columbia, SC 29201
  - **Links:** [Visit Website](https://midlandsfathers.com) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=1821+Hampton+St,+Columbia,+SC+29201)
  - **Next Step:** Schedule an intake appointment for SCDMV license restoration assistance.

- **SC Legal Services - Columbia Office**
  - **Services:** Free legal assistance for re-entry barriers, traffic court advocacy, and record expungement.
  - **Contact:** (803) 744-9430 | 2109 Bull St, Columbia, SC 29201
  - **Links:** [Visit Website](https://sclegal.org) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=2109+Bull+St,+Columbia,+SC+29201)
  - **Next Step:** Request legal aid consultation for pending Lexington County traffic matters.

- **LRADAC (Lexington/Richland Alcohol and Drug Abuse Council)**
  - **Services:** Outpatient recovery support, peer recovery coaching, and relapse prevention resources.
  - **Contact:** (803) 726-9300 | 2711 Colonial Dr, Columbia, SC 29203
  - **Links:** [Visit Website](https://lradac.org) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=2711+Colonial+Dr,+Columbia,+SC+29203)
  - **Next Step:** Connect with a peer recovery coach to complement your Oxford House leadership.

- **Welvista Headquarters (Prescription & Health Support)**
  - **Services:** Free prescription medication program for uninsured South Carolina residents.
  - **Contact:** (803) 933-9183 | 2700 Middleburg Dr, Suite 105, Columbia, SC 29204
  - **Links:** [Visit Website](https://welvista.org) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=2700+Middleburg+Dr,+Suite+105,+Columbia,+SC+29204)
  - **Next Step:** Submit prescription assistance enrollment for ongoing maintenance healthcare.

- **The COMET (Central Midlands Regional Transit)**
  - **Services:** Comprehensive public transit bus network across Columbia, West Columbia, Cayce, and industrial corridors.
  - **Contact:** (803) 255-7100 | Columbia Transit Hub
  - **Links:** [Visit Website](https://catchthecometsc.gov) | [Directions](https://maps.google.com/?q=Columbia+SC+COMET+Transit)
  - **Next Step:** Obtain a monthly bus pass and review route maps for Shop Road and Cayce job sites.

---

## 2. Fair-Chance Career Matches (Columbia Area)

1. **Carolina Industrial Maintenance Group**
   - **Role:** Maintenance Technician Apprentice / Commercial Cleaner
   - **Pay:** $16.50 – $19.50 / hr
   - **Shift:** Day Shift (7:30 AM – 4:00 PM, M–F)
   - **Match Reason:** Leverages mechanical and maintenance aptitude in a supportive daytime commercial environment.
   - **Apply:** [Apply Online / View Careers Page](https://www.indeed.com/jobs?q=maintenance+technician&l=Columbia%2C+SC)

2. **CMC Steel South Carolina**
   - **Role:** Mill Operator Trainee / Material Handler
   - **Pay:** $19.00 – $24.50 / hr
   - **Shift:** Day Shift (7:00 AM – 3:30 PM)
   - **Match Reason:** Fair-chance employer valuing industrial skills and mechanical machinery experience with strong benefits.
   - **Apply:** [Apply Online / View Careers Page](https://www.cmc.com/en-us/careers)

3. **Palmetto State Distribution Center**
   - **Role:** Order Selector / Inventory Staging Tech
   - **Pay:** $17.50 – $21.50 / hr
   - **Shift:** 1st Shift (7:00 AM – 3:30 PM)
   - **Match Reason:** Structured indoor warehouse environment on local transit routes; utilizes organizational and detail skills.
   - **Apply:** [Apply Online / View Careers Page](https://www.indeed.com/jobs?q=warehouse+order+selector&l=West+Columbia%2C+SC)

4. **Midlands Concrete & Paving Solutions**
   - **Role:** Concrete Finisher Helper / General Laborer
   - **Pay:** $18.00 – $23.00 / hr
   - **Shift:** 7:00 AM – 3:30 PM
   - **Match Reason:** Utilizes trade skills in construction and site work; second-chance friendly.
   - **Apply:** [Apply Online / View Careers Page](https://www.indeed.com/jobs?q=concrete+paving+laborer&l=Columbia%2C+SC)

---

## 3. Four-Week Action Checklist

- [ ] **Week 1: Immediate Triage & Legal Alignment**
  - Complete Turn90 case management check-in regarding Kershaw PPP agent contact.
  - Meet with Midlands Fatherhood Coalition for driver's license status review.
  - Secure COMET bus route schedule for daily commuting.

- [ ] **Week 2: Health & Recovery Fortification**
  - Submit Welvista enrollment application for ongoing prescription assistance.
  - Maintain active President leadership duties at Oxford House.
  - Work with Navigator to construct a personal budget using your accounting skills.

- [ ] **Week 3: Fair-Chance Employment Applications**
  - Apply to Carolina Industrial Maintenance Group and CMC Steel South Carolina.
  - Practice CBT mock interview responses focusing on positive accomplishments.
  - Coordinate interview transit routes via COMET bus lines.

- [ ] **Week 4: Onboarding & Long-Term Stability**
  - Finalize onboarding paperwork with selected drug-free employer.
  - Initiate $3,500 debt snowball repayment plan from First Shift / employment paychecks.
  - Celebrate 30-day recovery and stability milestone with Turn90 team.

CONFIDENTIAL — CASE MANAGEMENT REENTRY BRIEF — CHRISTOPHER BARRANCO Page 1
CASE MANAGEMENT REENTRY BRIEF
PARTICIPANT: Christopher David Barranco (DOB: 05/07/1985) | REVISED STATUS: HIGH RISK /
NEED
Current Placement: Oxford House Sober Living
(Elected President)
License Status: SUSPENDED (DUS 1st court
pending)
Legal Status: Active Probation (Kershaw
Violation Warrant)
Reentry Agency: Turn 90 Program (Stipend
Participant)
1. RISK PROFILE & CRIMINOGENIC DOMAINS
Christopher's revised LS/CMI assessment calculates a Section 1 Total Score of 21 / 43, officially elevating him to the
High Risk/Need category. This risk level indicates that his transition requires highly structured, high-intensity clinical
supervision. Per case management protocols, his high Criminal History subscore (7/8) is excluded from need
targeting, defining the following prioritized criminogenic need focus areas:
Primary Domain: Alcohol & Drug Problem (ADP Subscore: 5/8) [ELEVATED]: Christopher has a severe, chronic
history of substance use beginning at age 13, rooted in an alcoholic upbringing (Al-Anon attendee). His risk has
significantly escalated due to active drinking within the last 12 months, leading directly to job losses and a series of
arrests. Active recovery safeguards (Oxford House, Return for Christ, Calvary Chapel) are critical to prevent relapse,
which is his sole driver of criminality.
Secondary Domain: Education & Employment (EE Subscore: 5/9): Christopher completed his Associate's
Degree in Accounting at Midlands Technical College and is highly skilled in roofing, siding, heavy machinery
operation, and expert gutter machine installation. However, his current unemployment and lack of a stable payroll
history over the past year represent high risks. Because he is currently unemployed, his performance, peer, and
authority ratings are programmatically forced to 0, indicating unpracticed workplace behavioral skills.
Tertiary Domain: Procriminal Attitude (PA Subscore: 1/4) [ELEVATED]: Despite displaying profound verbal
remorse, Christopher committed multiple property, drug, and child neglect offenses within the last 12 months
(shoplifting in March 2025, probation violation in December 2025). This active property offending scores Item 36
(Supportive of Crime) as YES, which programmatically forces Item 42 (Criminal Attitude) to YES in Section 1.8 AP
(Antisocial Pattern), raising his AP subscore to 2/4. Case managers must target this active supportive behavior.
2. BEHAVIORAL INDICATORS & THINKING PATTERNS
Christopher's behavior reflects a complex interplay between highly developed prosocial strengths and severe
relapse-driven antisocial defaults:
• Justifying / Minimizing: Christopher displays a severe justification distortion regarding his adult criminal history.
During the diagnostic interview, he claimed 'none' adult convictions, whereas his official Intelius background report
documents over ten convictions for forgery, shoplifting, grand larceny, drug possession, and child neglect. Staff must
gently confront this gap with collateral records to build honest self-reflection.

-- 1 of 4 --

CONFIDENTIAL — CASE MANAGEMENT REENTRY BRIEF — CHRISTOPHER BARRANCO Page 2
• Relapse-Driven 'Cut Off' Pattern: Christopher has a long-standing history of quitting work or being terminated
abruptly, admitting that 'every job I've ever lost was because of my own fault relapsing... starting with drinking.'
Drinking acts as his cognitive 'Cut Off' coping default under acute financial or emotional distress.
• Prosocial Leadership (Protective Strength): In a remarkable strength, Christopher was elected President of his
Oxford House and serves as an active usher/chef for family dinners at Calvary Chapel. He has strong self-regulation
habits when sober—setting explicit plans and goals, writing them down, and reviewing them regularly. Staff must
leverage this leadership capacity to reinforce his self-esteem.

-- 2 of 4 --

CONFIDENTIAL — CASE MANAGEMENT REENTRY BRIEF — CHRISTOPHER BARRANCO Page 3
3. TRAJECTORY & PATTERN OVER TIME
Christopher's legal involvement began at age 11 with an arrest in Florida for trespassing, establishing early-onset
juvenile delinquency (4 juvenile convictions). In adulthood, he developed an entrenched, 20-year cycle of non-violent
property offending, drug possession, and domestic conflicts. His criminal career has heavily escalated recently,
culminating in child neglect convictions (2021) and active probation violations (December 2025). The cycle we are
interrupting is a chronic, substance-fueled collapse where active drinking instantly dissolves his high intellectual and
professional capabilities, sending him back into property crime and community supervision failures.
4. ACUTE / EMERGENCY NEEDS
• Active Probation Violation Warrant: Immediate administrative coordination is required with his probation agent
(Burgess) and Kershaw County PPP regarding his active December 12, 2025 probation violation warrant to prevent
sudden re-arrest.
• Transitional Income & Financial Crisis: Currently has 0 active income, relying entirely on food stamps and his
small Turn 90 stipend. This financial strain is an active relapse trigger.
• Active DUS Charge: Has an outstanding pending traffic court status in Lexington for Driving Under Suspension
(DUS 1st) stemming from March 2025.
5. STRUCTURAL STABILITY FACTORS
• Oxford House Placement (High Stability): Extremely stable and supportive sober-living environment. His role as
President provides massive structural accountability.
• Severe Physical Trauma (Loss of Lung): He was shot in the chest during a drug dispute in his past, resulting in
the surgical loss of half of his left lung. This remains a permanent physical vulnerability and a chronic PTSD/anxiety
trigger.
• Transportation Barrier: Suspended driver's license due to traffic debt. All travel relies strictly on public transit or
sober-living peers.
• High Debt Load: Owed $3,500 to Landmark in Lexington and receives harassing creditor calls, causing severe
anxiety.
6. LEGAL & PLACEMENT CONSTRAINTS
Christopher has an active probation status out of Kershaw and Lexington Counties, with documented supervision
failure history. His suspended license restricts physical transit, and he must avoid any workplace placements where
drugs or alcohol are present on-site. He has no Sex Offender Registry requirements.
7. RESPONSIVITY & ENGAGEMENT PROFILE
• Trauma-Informed, Collaborative Style: Due to his severe physical trauma (gunshot wound, loss of half a lung)
and childhood trauma (alcoholic parent, running away), staff must utilize a highly supportive, calm, and collaborative
coaching style. Aggressive, directive, or confrontational tactics will trigger survival-based defensiveness or anxiety.
• Leverage Accounting Background for Debt Management: Capitalize on his Midlands Tech Accounting
Associate's degree. Involve him directly in co-creating his budget and a structured 'Debt Snowball' plan to manage his
$3,500 Landmark debt, which will reduce his financial relapse triggers.

-- 3 of 4 --

CONFIDENTIAL — CASE MANAGEMENT REENTRY BRIEF — CHRISTOPHER BARRANCO Page 4
• Safe, Drug-Free Employment Matching: Leverage his expert gutter installation, roofing, and heavy machinery
certifications. Placements must be rigorously vetted to ensure they are 100% drug-free. Christopher explicitly notes
that past jobs with drug-using crews triggered his relapses; matching him with prosocial, sober work environments is
mandatory for his recovery.
• Address Denial and Minimization Supportive: Use Cognitive Behavioral Therapy (CBT) to supportively address
his minimization of his adult record. Connect his admitting of past relapses to the Intelius collateral records, helping
him bridge the narrative gaps with accountability and self-forgiveness.

-- 4 of 4 --
